findings.title: Backfill suffix match must be exact and case-sensitive, not LIKE
findings.why_it_matters: LIKE is case-insensitive with _/% wildcards; it matched child hassette.apps.api.Api for instance api.
findings.chosen: Specify exact substr-based suffix and prefix tests in D1; test api/Api and my_app cases.

findings.title: The SQL author rule has no test pinning it to both logger-name eras
findings.why_it_matters: Rows rewritten are almost all v0.59.0-shaped names that current code cannot produce.
findings.chosen: D1 pins the rule for v0.59.0 and current logger-name shapes, module loggers, py.warnings and NULL instance_name.

findings.title: The backfill discards stored true authors on rows written by unreleased builds
findings.why_it_matters: Post-#3173 rows hold the true author; D1 re-derives it, mislabelling warnings and getChild loggers.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: rows written by unreleased builds since #3173 get the derived author, not their stamped one, for up to 30 days.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: rows written by unreleased builds since #3173 get the derived author, not their stamped one, for up to 30 days.

findings.title: Migration 015's stated reason for a rebuild is wrong, and its shape is left open
findings.why_it_matters: SQLite can ADD COLUMN NOT NULL with a DEFAULT; a rebuild would drop three indexes.
findings.recommended: A: Specify the in-place shape in D1 and correct the Assumed bullet: `ADD COLUMN author TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'framework' CHECK (author IN ('app','framework'))`, `UPDATE` by the rule, `DROP COLUMN source_tier`. No index changes.
findings.chosen: A: Specify the in-place shape in D1 and correct the Assumed bullet: `ADD COLUMN author TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'framework' CHECK (author IN ('app','framework'))`, `UPDATE` by the rule, `DROP COLUMN source_tier`. No index changes.

findings.title: The ERROR-and-above set has no layer-correct source
findings.why_it_matters: LOG_LEVELS lives in web/dependencies.py and holds every level; core importing it inverts layers.
findings.chosen: Move LOG_LEVELS to hassette_wire.literals beside LogLevel; derive ERROR+ names numerically; web imports from there.

findings.title: Old app lines logged outside bound context read framework and hide below ERROR
findings.why_it_matters: NULL instance_name on old app lines makes the rule label them framework.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: old app lines logged outside bound context read `framework` and need the opt-in below ERROR for up to 30 days.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: old app lines logged outside bound context read `framework` and need the opt-in below ERROR for up to 30 days.

findings.title: No way back after the migration
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: users who roll back. 015 drops source_tier; rollback means deleting the DB.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: migration 015 is one-way; rolling back past it means deleting the telemetry DB.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: migration 015 is one-way; rolling back past it means deleting the telemetry DB.

findings.title: Migration 015 rewrites every log row under the 120 s startup timeout
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: high log volume on slow storage; first start may time out.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: a very large log table on slow storage may time out the first start after upgrading, and the next start completes.
findings.chosen: B: Accept as a known limitation: a very large log table on slow storage may time out the first start after upgrading, and the next start completes.

findings.title: No index supports the new default log predicate
findings.why_it_matters: Audience assumption: large framework-DEBUG-heavy tables; default query walks the timestamp index.
findings.recommended: B: Accept as a known limitation: the default log query scans by timestamp and can slow down on very large tables dominated by framework DEBUG lines.
